messages.content: Explain paradoxes accessibly. Identify the contradiction, then resolve or describe why it can't be resolved.
Explain the Ship of Theseus paradox and how a modern philosopher might resolve it.

message.content:
The **Ship of Theseus paradox** is a classic philosophical puzzle, often attributed to Plutarch, that questions whether an object that has had all its components replaced remains fundamentally the same object.

### The Paradox Explained
The story goes: The hero Theseus sails on a ship. Over time, every wooden plank rots and is replaced, one by one. Eventually, **every single part** has been swapped out. The question is:  
- **Is it still the same ship?**  
- If it is, what about a second ship built from all the discarded original planks—**is that the "real" ship?**  

The paradox highlights the tension between:
- **Material continuity** (the physical substance)
- **Structural/form continuity** (the design or pattern)
- **Identity over time** (what makes something "the same" despite change)

---

### How a Modern Philosopher Might Resolve It
Modern philosophy approaches this through several lenses, often rejecting the idea that identity is a single, simple fact.

#### 1. **Perdurantism (Four-Dimensionalism)**
This view, common in contemporary metaphysics, treats objects as **spatio-temporal worms**—they exist through time as a "time-slice" at each moment.  
- The ship at \( t_1 \) is a different entity from the ship at \( t_2 \), but they are stages of the **same ship-object**.
